claim: LLM-judge funniness correlates only rho 0.17-0.27 with humans on Oogiri comedy and scores topically-irrelevant jokes highly.
A trained role-play reward model (CharacterRM) scoring persona fidelity reaches Pearson 0.631 with human judgment versus GPT-4's 0.375.
In content-controlled style discrimination, humans agree strongly on formal/informal style (0.90) and BERT style measures reach 0.77-1.00, but simple/complex style is ambiguous (Fleiss kappa 0.17).
Among text-style-transfer metrics, style-strength signals such as classifier confidence and Jensen-Shannon divergence achieve the best human correlations (about 0.51-0.67), well above BLEU/ROUGE.
A meta-analysis of text-style-transfer evaluation finds that only a handful of automatic style-strength metrics have ever been validated against human experiments (a validation gap).
Authorship/style embeddings tend to encode topic/content rather than pure style, and only conversation-level content control yields representations that track style independent of content.
Style embeddings beat a GPT-4o judge on scripted/spoken registers (81.5% vs 67.7%) while the LLM judge wins on fiction/academic prose, so neither dominates for authorship/style attribution.
Dialogue-NLI recasts persona consistency as entailment/contradiction against persona sentences, producing the reproducible NLI-based persona-consistency C-score.
GPT-4 judges reach about 85% agreement with human preferences on open-ended answer quality (exceeding the 81% human-human rate) but exhibit position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases.
When ChatGPT scores text-style-transfer outputs, style-transfer-strength is its weakest dimension at 31.2% dataset-level accuracy, below a dedicated style classifier.
The best LLM evaluators identify which persona a line belongs to at only about 69% accuracy versus 90.8% for humans.
LLM judges recognize their own generations, and a model's self-preference bias is linearly correlated with that self-recognition ability.
LLM judges assign higher scores to lower-perplexity (more familiar-to-the-model) text independent of human ratings.
A panel of heterogeneous cross-family LLM judges correlates with humans better than a single GPT-4 (Cohen's kappa 0.76 vs 0.63) and reduces self-preference variance at about 7x lower cost.
LLM-judge position bias is severe (reordering candidates can flip verdicts), and Balanced-Position with Multiple-Evidence Calibration is a validated mitigation.
When shortcut cues are injected, LLM-judge verdicts shift but their chain-of-thought acknowledges the cue about 0% of the time, rationalizing decisions as clarity/fluency instead.
Best-Worst Scaling reaches split-half reliability rho 0.98 versus rating scales' 0.95 for a subtle graded attribute, using about 30% as many annotations.
For LLM judges on stylistic attributes, pairwise comparative assessment beats absolute prompt-scoring by large margins (coherence Spearman 51.2 vs 14.5).

A classifier-confidence style-strength metric correlates with human style-intensity only about 0.54-0.56, and pairwise human scoring gives no inter-rater-reliability gain over absolute for style intensity.
Style classifiers hinge on a few pivot words: a bag-of-pivot-words classifier scores 88.4% versus a CNN's 93.0%, so classifier style-strength is largely lexical and gameable by swapping keywords.
ASAP active pair-sampling reaches target error with about 3x fewer comparisons than alternatives (7,065 vs 10,550).
LLM-judge pairwise preferences are significantly non-transitive, and fitting a Bradley-Terry model over round-robin comparisons stabilizes otherwise-fragile rankings.
Ditto self-alignment fine-tunes one conditioned model to role-play 4,000 characters with consistent identity across multi-turn dialogue, beating open-source role-play baselines.
Persona-Aware Contrastive Learning (contrasting responses with vs without role characteristics) raises Character-Consistency on CharacterEval by about 3-3.7% for 7B models.
An SFT-then-PPO pipeline with rewards discriminating hierarchical style-intensity levels lands text about 64% closer to a target readability than GPT-4o-mini.

Naively merging multiple task LoRAs causes cross-task interference and catastrophic forgetting; LoRI freezes A and sparsifies B into near-orthogonal subspaces to restore per-task performance with far fewer parameters.
Ranking training data by stylistic consistency shows that as little as 0.7% of style-consistent data can match or beat fine-tuning on the full set.
LIMA fine-tunes on only 1,000 curated style-consistent examples with no RL and is preferred-or-tied against GPT-4 43% of the time.
Identity/persona drift over multi-turn conversation grows with model scale, and assigning a persona does not reliably prevent it.
Standard cross-entropy SFT collapses output diversity (generative-distribution entropy 0.42 vs 0.76 under entropy-regularized GEM).
Assigning ChatGPT a persona increased toxicity up to 6x over the default across roughly 500K generations, with some demographic entities targeted about 3x more.
Adopting socio-demographic personas silently degraded LLM reasoning accuracy by 70%+ on some datasets, with significant drops on 80%+ of 24 datasets even while the model overtly denies stereotyping.
CoMPosT operationalizes caricature as low individuation plus high exaggeration and finds GPT-4 persona simulations of marginalized and political groups are the most susceptible.
GPT-3.5/GPT-4 persona portrayals of non-white, non-male groups contain higher rates of racial stereotypes than human-written portrayals from identical prompts.
African American English dialect prompting elicited covert stereotypes more negative than any experimentally recorded human stereotype, and human-preference alignment worsened the covert/overt gap.
A self-chat benchmark shows measurable persona/instruction drift within 8 conversational rounds in models up to LLaMA2-70B, attributed to attention decay.
Co-writing with the aligned InstructGPT (but not base GPT-3) significantly reduced content diversity and increased inter-author homogenization.
Across n-gram and Sentence-BERT measures, RLHF markedly reduces per-input output diversity relative to SFT and base models.
